job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: The Earth is surrounded by a vast blanket of air called the atmosphere, which extends hundreds of kilometers above the surface. While we often see clouds floating in the lower parts, the atmosphere continues far beyond them into space. This air is a mixture of many gases. Nitrogen is the most abundant gas, making up about 78 percent of the air we breathe, while oxygen accounts for only 21 percent. Even though oxygen is vital for human survival, its lower percentage compared to nitrogen is a scientific fact. Air also contains invisible water vapor, which is the gaseous form of water. This amount of water vapor in the air is known as humidity. It is important to understand that humidity is always present in the air, even on clear, sunny days when it is not raining. Rain only occurs when this water vapor cools down and condenses into droplets. Therefore, humidity is simply the presence of moisture in the air, whereas rain is a specific event where that moisture falls to the ground.

items.evidence: While we often see clouds floating in the lower parts, the atmosphere continues far beyond them into space.
items.q: A plane flies higher than all the clouds. Where is the plane now?
options: Outside the atmosphere, out in space
At the top edge of the atmosphere
Only a few kilometres below space
items.explain: The atmosphere goes far beyond the clouds, hundreds of kilometres up, so the plane is still in it.

wrong.why: thinks the atmosphere ends where clouds end
thinks clouds mark the outer edge of the air
ignores that air extends hundreds of kilometres up

items.evidence: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas, making up about 78 percent of the air we breathe, while oxygen accounts for only 21 percent.
items.q: Imagine 100 litres of air. Which gas would fill most of it?
items.explain: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air; oxygen is only 21 percent.

wrong.why: thinks the most important gas must be the most abundant
thinks air is only oxygen and carbon dioxide
picks the nearby number meant for oxygen

items.evidence: It is important to understand that humidity is always present in the air, even on clear, sunny days when it is not raining.
items.q: It has not rained for a week and the sky is clear. What about water in the air?
options: There is still invisible water vapour
There is none, since no rain fell
There is some, but only inside clouds
There is none, as sunshine dried it
items.explain: Humidity is always in the air, even on clear, sunny days with no rain.

wrong.why: thinks humidity is the same as rain
thinks water in air exists only as visible clouds
guesses that sunny weather removes all moisture

items.evidence: Therefore, humidity is simply the presence of moisture in the air, whereas rain is a specific event where that moisture falls to the ground.
items.q: How is humidity different from rain?
options: Humidity is vapour in air; rain is falling drops
Humidity is light rain; rain is heavy rain
Humidity comes after rain; rain comes first
Humidity is a liquid; rain is a gas
items.explain: Humidity is water vapour present in air; rain is when that moisture falls to the ground.

wrong.why: thinks humidity is just a kind of rain
reverses cause and effect between vapour and rain
mixes up the gas and liquid forms of water
